world.geography: United States, Washington (ten eastern Washington counties)

driver: A population defined by a lasting trait is counted from records that show the trait only through events logged while each unit is observed; the fully observed units cannot stand in for the briefly observed, because staying observed is selected on the trait, so each recorded unit is counted as one over the share of fully observed trait-holders recorded within a window of its own length, measured on their time to a first event, and carrying the fully observed units' rate to every unit, even within the visible groups, overstates exactly the segments whose units come and go.
driver_concrete: Adult members with a serious mental illness or an opioid use disorder appear in the claims only through services billed while they were enrolled; the members enrolled all year are fully observed but are not a sample of the membership, because the farmworkers who enrol for a harvest have the conditions about half as often, so each identified member is counted as 1 over the share of the full-year members with the condition identified within the same number of months, and carrying the full-year prevalence to every member, eligibility group by group, overstates Yakima and fails it on two standards it meets (figures fixed at build).
stump: A strong analyst completes each county's members with each condition, as NP-31 2.5 requires, with the prevalence its members enrolled all year show within each eligibility group, carried to all the group's members, and designates Adams, Douglas, Franklin, Grant, Okanogan and Yakima, because the seasonal expansion adults and parents in Yakima's short spells have the conditions about half as often as the members who stay enrolled; counted for the months each identified member was enrolled, Yakima meets all three standards. A weaker analyst counts the identified members and designates Douglas and Okanogan.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms NPPES, the claims and the enrollment spans, reads every field and NP-31 correctly and completes each county's count of members with a serious mental illness and with an opioid use disorder, as NP-31 2.5 requires (every member who has the condition, identified or not), with the prevalence its members enrolled all year show within each eligibility group (the stage-4 leak reader's route on the first design), designates Adams, Douglas, Franklin, Grant, Okanogan and Yakima; carrying the county's full-year prevalence whole files the same six; counting the identified members files Douglas and Okanogan.
domain_test: Need is each county's number of adult members with a serious mental illness and with an opioid use disorder, estimated the way claims-based epidemiology corrects case identification for the length of observation: the sensitivity of a k-month lookback window measured on members observed all year, applied to each identified member's own window, because continuously enrolled Medicaid members are sicker than the members who churn; with retail or school nouns no enrolment is selected on a lasting condition recorded only through billed services, and no standard counts people the record does not show.

differentiation.task231: task231 estimates the exited share of a register's silent units from follow-up that reaches active units more often than exited ones; task458 counts members with a lasting condition from claims that record it only while each member is enrolled, correcting each identified member for the sensitivity of its own window measured on the fully observed members, because the fully observed are a selected group.
differentiation.task445: task445 completes a period's holdings for reporters whose reports have not arrived; task458 counts a population whose trait the record shows only through events during each unit's observation, so the shortfall sits with units observed briefly, not with units still to report.
differentiation.task456: task456 estimates each region's share of full ICU hospital-days with a latent class model of three conflicting feeds, no feed a record of the outcome; task458 has one record of each condition that is complete for members observed all year and censored for members enrolled briefly, and counts each identified member over its window's sensitivity: no latent class, no feed error rates.
differentiation.task457: task457 aligns each disclosure with the register's payments made by the day it was submitted and weights a matched-line ratio by its credibility; task458 counts members with a condition from claims censored by enrollment, each identified member over its window's sensitivity: no register, no reporting ratio, no credibility weighting; the two share only the ETL pack's genres (a policy PDF, a dictionary, CSV extracts).
differentiation.task448: task448 completes a register missing whole lenders from a second list whose capture depends on the recording route, estimated within route strata on the lenders both lists hold; task458 has one list (the claims) whose capture of a lasting condition depends on how long each member was enrolled, measured on the members observed all year and applied to each identified member's own window, and its trap is the selected reference population (the full-year members' prevalence carried to the seasonal enrollees), not a pooled capture.
differentiation.task458: the first design's golden (the full-year prevalence standardized by eligibility group) is this design's default path: the seasonal members' lower prevalence makes it file the six, and the decisive step moves from standardizing the reference population to not using it as the seasonal members' stand-in at all.

lineage.fate: solved at stage 4 by the isolated leak reader (Sonnet, medium) at loop 0: the full-year prevalence standardized by eligibility group was a reflex once the group mix showed, so the stump was re-centred on the seasonal members' own records
lineage.driver: A population defined by a lasting trait is counted from records that show the trait only through events logged while each unit is observed; the rate is measured on the fully observed units, but full observation depends on a grouping that also drives the trait, so the fully observed units' rate has to be taken within each group and carried to each group's units, and carrying it whole overstates exactly the segments whose units come and go.

imperfect keys: rendering NPIs present on some encounters and absent on others, member numbers reissued at re-enrollment and tied by a person number, practice against mailing addresses, ZIP codes spanning two counties
documentation that has to be read: the taxonomy code list, the standard's definitions, claim frequency and place-of-service codes
